notes: §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR10c: "If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed" (its compile-time half is SR7, "no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure"). The 1985 text defines neither "applicable" nor "appropriate", and two final adjudications read it opposite ways (2026-11-12, kb/Work PB5413 amendment 1: reading A, a mode procedure is applicable to a statement of any file that can be open in that mode; 2026-11-14, op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json q1: reading B, only a mode in which the statement's condition can arise). So it is implementor latitude, and WiseOwl COBOL takes reading A as a DOCUMENTED LATITUDE CHOICE (kb/Work PB5591; docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.5; docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D31(a)): reading B would refuse CCVS-85 SQ148A, GnuCOBOL 3.2 -std=cobol85 enforces none of the mandatory-phrase rules and so does not decide, and rejecting legal source is the worse harm. ExceptionPhraseRequirement.HasApplicableUse implements it: a declarative naming the file, or one for an open mode the file can be open in (EXTEND only for a file that can be opened EXTEND, kb/Work PB5413), refuses COBOL6826 otherwise. The witness (pb5591_indexed_output_use_excuses_phrases_85) runs at --std 85: the statement with no phrase is accepted under the one mode declarative, and at run time the procedure takes the logic-error status the statement raises in that mode (47, 48 or 49), matching the expectation derived from the text. The adjudication's probe (refute-rs-05/e4.cob (re-run this session: held-adj/q1/e4.cob)) observed: compiles with no diagnostic; AFTER 10; exit 0; no procedure ran (re-run this session on the pinned binary); under reading A that is the conforming result. Previous verdict: PARTIAL, held on reading B. Recorded 2026-11-14 by records-85-held from the final held-row adjudication (op-20261114/held-adjudicated.json).

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993; the C282 and C283 flags) reworded b and c: the USE procedure is now the one 'associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1', and b spells out that after imperative-statement-1 'control is transferred to the end of the READ statement and the NOT AT END phrase, if specified, is ignored'. It kept the requirement that differs from 2023. 1985 c: 'If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed' (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR10), with 'The INVALID KEY phrase or the AT END phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1' (§1985:IX.4.5.3 SR7). 2023 d): 'any applicable at end exception processing statements are executed. If there are no applicable at end exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the READ statement' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24); 14.9.30.3 has no such syntax rule, so a READ with neither AT END nor a USE procedure, which 1985 refuses, is accepted. GR24 a) also adds 'if enabled, the EC-I-O-AT-END exception condition is set to exist' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24). The rest is carried: the trigger and status ('an optional input file is not present or that no next or previous logical record exists, the I-O status value associated with file-name-1 is set to '10', the at end condition exists', §2023:14.9.30.4 GR21; §2023:9.1.13.4 GR1), AT END taking precedence over the USE procedure (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24c; §2023:14.9.49.4 GR6 'unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence'), the USE declarative as the applicable exception processing statement (§2023:9.1.12 GR2), the return after it to 'an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR7), and 'execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24).
